results.reason: The memo quotes §2.2's automatic five-year renewal and the 270/240-day notice requirement. It calculates the window as June 3 – July 3, 2026, which is effectively a 30-day window. It explains that missing it locks Harrowgate into a five-year Renewal Term through February 2032.

The memo quotes §3.1 (all glass and PET containers, any beverage, worldwide, including Affiliates). It contrasts this with the Term Sheet's amber-glass, beer, U.S./Canada scope. It treats Harrowgate as bound by the executed text, noting that out-of-scope purchases would breach §3.1.

The memo quotes Recital C (14% notice received August 3, 2026). It computes the September 2, 2026 objection deadline under §5.4, before the September 21 amendment date. It concludes the increase is deemed accepted.

The memo explains that Amendment §2.1 replaced §11.2, removing recall costs and limiting the indemnity carve-out to IP claims under §9.1(c). It states that recall and product-liability exposure is now subject to the six-month fees cap.

The memo identifies new §14.4, which allows assignment without consent to Affiliates or to change-of-control successors notwithstanding §14.3. It notes Harrowgate would be stuck if Supplier were acquired by a competitor. It notes the arrangement is one-sided because Customer still needs consent under §14.3.
The Order of Precedence Note states that §15.2 places written amendments first and that Amendment No. 1 controls over the original §11.2.
The memo states the §11.1 cap is 'the fees paid by Customer in the six months before the claim arose.'
The memo is addressed to [Partner] and organized issue by issue. Each issue gives a 'Where' citation to the document and section, plus a recommended fix.
The memo proposes specific language, including a narrowed §3.1, a restored §11.2, and a revised §14.4 with conditions.
The memo concludes the objection window has closed and there is no contractual basis to challenge the increase now.
The memo does not treat the Term Sheet as governing. It recommends amending §3.1 and treats the executed scope as currently binding.
